name: Processor D
justification: Measured with the official transpilation, the JW-4q and tapered-2q hardware-efficient circuits needed zero SWAPs and the same CX count on Processors A, B and D (JW-4q depth 1: 3 CX; tapered-2q depth 1: 1 CX), because their linear CZ chain embeds in all three graphs. For this ansatz the bottleneck is therefore CX count and circuit depth, not routing, and the 4-to-2 qubit reduction cut CX from 3 to 1. D keeps the chain (edges 0-1, 1-2, 2-3) so chemistry circuits pay nothing, and adds edges 3-0 and 0-2 so that every pair except 1-3 is directly coupled and the farthest pair is two hops instead of three; on a plain 4-qubit line the far-pair Bell circuit cost 7 CX in our test. Error rates equal the official 0.001, 0.005 and 0.01 because the rules forbid better values. The trade-off is two extra couplers, with calibration and crosstalk costs the noise model ignores, for no gain on the required chemistry circuits.
